items.followUp: What is a mole? Calculate the mass of 2 moles of NaOH and state the mass of NaOH needed to prepare 500 cm³ of a 1 M solution.

rubric.why: A mole is defined by the number of elementary entities it contains.
rubric.description: Defines a mole as the amount of substance containing Avogadro’s number of particles.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the number and reference to particles/entities; 1 mark for either element alone.

rubric.why: One mole of NaOH has a mass of 40 g, so this amount gives a 1 M solution when the final solution volume is 1 L.
rubric.description: States the required mass of NaOH and final solution volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 40 g NaOH and 1 mark for making the final solution volume 1 L (or equivalent).

rubric.why: These are useful preparation details but the question’s four marks are allocated to the definition and the mass-volume calculation.
rubric.how: No separate marks; include these details in the model answer.

modelAnswer: A mole is the amount of substance that contains 6.022 × 10²³ elementary entities (such as atoms, molecules or ions).
The molar mass of NaOH is 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g mol⁻¹.
Weigh 40 g of NaOH and dissolve it in a small amount of distilled water.
Transfer the solution to a 1 L volumetric flask and add distilled water up to the mark; mix well.

items.followUp: What are the four blocks of the modern periodic table, and how is an element assigned to a block?

rubric.why: Block classification depends on the subshell receiving the differentiating (last) electron.
rubric.description: States the basis for dividing elements into blocks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the block to the subshell into which the last electron enters.

rubric.why: The four block names complete the classification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying all four blocks.

modelAnswer: The blocks are divisions of the modern periodic table based on the subshell into which the last electron of an atom enters.
They are called the s-, p-, d- and f-blocks.

items.followUp: What is shielding effect, and how does it affect the attraction between the nucleus and a valence electron?

rubric.why: Effective nuclear charge is the net positive charge experienced by an electron.
rubric.description: Identifies effective nuclear charge as the net positive charge experienced by an electron.

rubric.why: The effective charge is reduced from the full nuclear charge because inner electrons shield the outer electron.
rubric.description: Explains that inner electrons reduce the nuclear attraction through shielding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating the reduced charge to shielding by inner electrons.

modelAnswer: Effective nuclear charge is the net positive charge experienced by an electron in an atom.
It is less than the total nuclear charge because inner-shell electrons shield the outer electron from the nucleus.

items.followUp: Define a polar covalent bond and state how its shared pair of electrons is distributed.

rubric.why: A coordinate covalent bond forms when both electrons in the shared pair come from one atom.
rubric.description: States that the shared electron pair is donated by one atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the single-atom donation of the pair.

rubric.why: The donated pair is shared between the donor and acceptor atoms, forming a covalent bond.
rubric.description: States that the donated pair is shared with another atom to form the bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the sharing/bond formation aspect.

modelAnswer: A coordinate covalent bond is a covalent bond in which both electrons of the shared pair are donated by one atom.
The donating atom provides a lone pair to an atom or ion that can accept it.

items.followUp: What type of force holds neighbouring water molecules together, and between which particles does it act?

rubric.why: Intermolecular forces are forces of attraction.
rubric.description: Identifies the force as an attraction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is an attractive force.

rubric.why: The defining feature is that the force acts between separate molecules.
rubric.description: Identifies the particles between which the force acts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it acts between molecules.

modelAnswer: Intermolecular force is the force of attraction between molecules.

items.followUp: Define boiling and freezing in terms of changes of state.

rubric.why: Evaporation is the change from liquid to vapour at the surface of a liquid.
rubric.description: Defines evaporation as liquid changing into vapour.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct change of state.

rubric.why: Condensation is the change from vapour to liquid.
rubric.description: Defines condensation as vapour changing into liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct reverse change of state.

modelAnswer: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour from its surface.
Condensation is the change of vapour into liquid.

items.followUp: Why does the rate of evaporation increase when a liquid is heated?

rubric.why: Heating increases the kinetic energy of the liquid molecules.
rubric.description: Explains that molecules gain kinetic energy at higher temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the increase in molecular kinetic energy.

rubric.why: More energetic molecules can overcome attractions and enter the vapour, increasing vapour pressure.
rubric.description: Links the greater molecular energy to more molecules escaping and a higher vapour pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the escape of more molecules and the resulting rise in vapour pressure.

modelAnswer: At higher temperature, liquid molecules have greater kinetic energy.
More molecules can overcome intermolecular attractions and escape into the vapour phase.
The increased number of vapour molecules produces a higher vapour pressure.

items.followUp: Define molarity and calculate the molarity of a solution containing 0.5 mol of solute in 250 cm³ of solution.

rubric.why: Molarity is the amount of solute, in moles, per unit volume of solution.
rubric.description: Defines molarity as moles of solute per unit volume of solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: The formula expresses the definition quantitatively, with volume in dm³ (or L).
rubric.description: Gives the molarity formula and an appropriate unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the formula with a suitable concentration unit.

modelAnswer: Molarity is the number of moles of solute dissolved per dm³ (or litre) of solution.
M = n/V, where n is the number of moles of solute and V is the volume of solution in dm³.
The unit of molarity is mol dm⁻³ (or mol L⁻¹).
